extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: A comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite comprising 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines and four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional), designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.rai:dataCollection: C-EVAL comprises multiple-choice questions collected from four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional tests across 52 diverse disciplines. Questions mostly come from mock exams as PDF or Microsoft Word documents that are further processed. The benchmark includes 13,948 multiple-choice exam questions spanning subjects ranging from humanities to science and engineering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exam questions from PDF or Microsoft Word documents covering middle school, high school, college, and professional level subjects. For college level, 25 representative subjects were selected from 13 official categories of undergraduate majors listed by the Ministry of Education in China. For professional level, 12 subjects were chosen referring to the official national vocational qualification directory in China.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were parsed from various formats (PDF, Word documents, web pages) into structured format, either automatically or manually by authors. All questions underwent several rounds of human validation by authors. For explanation data, GPT-4 was prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for ground-truth answers, which were then manually revised by authors to obtain final explanations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All LATEX notations were ensured to be compiled without syntax errors during validation rounds.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Authors of the paper served as annotators
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate step-by-step explanations for development set examples, which were then manually revised
extraction.rai:dataBiases: C-EVAL is designed to address geographical biases in English benchmarks by focusing on Chinese context, culture, history, and laws. English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness that are not covered.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: C-EVAL aims to guide developers in preparing LLMs to function in more complex scenarios beyond casual conversational bots, particularly for Chinese users. It helps analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models and foster their development for Chinese users.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: C-EVAL is designed for evaluating advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It can be used as a whole or in subsets to assess certain model abilities of interest and analyze important strengths and limitations of foundation models. The test split labels are kept private to ensure fair use, with users submitting predictions to obtain test accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were standardized to exactly four choices by eliminating questions with fewer than four options and randomly dropping incorrect choices for questions with more than four options. Questions were randomly split into development set (5 exemplars per subject), validation set, and test set with a 1:9 validation-to-test ratio. Development split was augmented with chain-of-thought explanations generated by GPT-4 and then manually validated.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF and Microsoft Word documents were converted to text format. Questions were parsed into structured format (automatically when possible, otherwise manually). Complex mathematical notations were manually converted to standard LaTeX format. Standard data preprocessing pipeline applied including deduplication and cleaning. Multiple rounds of human validation performed, with LaTeX notation syntax verification.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: LLMs intended for use in a Chinese environment should be evaluated on their knowledge of Chinese users' primary interests, such as Chinese culture, history, and laws, as well as other competencies unique in Chinese society. In contrast, English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We also note that, C-EVAL, along with all the English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We believe that the evaluation of LLMs should transcend the scope of casual conversational bots, guiding developers in preparing LLMs to function in more complex scenarios. This was the primary motivation behind the creation of C-EVAL, a challenging evaluation suite... We anticipate C-EVAL will help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models, and foster their development and growth for Chinese users.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present C-EVAL, the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context... In addition to its use as a whole, we envision C-EVAL as a suite of benchmarks, subsets of which could be separately utilized to assess certain model abilities of interest and analyze important strengths and limitations of foundation models... While ground-truth labels of the development and validation splits are released, we keep the labels of the test split private. This is to ensure the fair use of the C-EVAL, as the C-EVAL data may unconsciously be included in pretraining data due to web crawling.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: All the questions in C-EVAL are processed to include exactly four choices. Most of the original questions were accompanied by four choices already, and we eliminate questions with fewer than four options and randomly drop incorrect choices for questions with more than four options... randomly split the questions into a development set, a validation set, and a test set within each subject. The development split per subject consists of five exemplars to facilitate few-shot evaluation... The validation and test set are created with a 1:9 ratio... we first prompt GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanation to explain the ground-truth answer

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: PDF documents are initially processed into text. All questions are subsequently parsed – automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors – into a structured format... we manually convert them into standard LATEX formats... All questions also go through the standard data preprocessing pipeline, such as deduplication and cleaning. Following this, the questions undergo several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all the LATEX notations are ensured to be complied without syntax errors.
